q8.answer: The merge is guarded: it matches on order_id and overwrites only when the incoming updated_at is strictly greater than the stored one. Older or identical versions are no-ops. Staging is also deduped to keep the max updated_at per order_id before the merge.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse table etl.state (one row, pipeline='orders', column hwm_updated_at). It is set to GREATEST(current hwm, batch_max), where batch_max is the max updated_at actually extracted (never now()). The write happens inside the same warehouse transaction as the merge, at commit; an empty batch leaves it unchanged.

q10.answer: Extraction goes into stg.orders, which dashboards never read. The merge into dw.orders and the hwm update happen in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards see the last committed state: the whole night or none of it. This relies on the warehouse supporting multi-statement transactions with snapshot isolation, which is an open question. The fallback is a shadow table plus an atomic swap.

q11.answer: Each attempt truncates stg.orders first, so leftover staged data from the failed attempt is discarded. The retry re-reads the hwm from etl.state, which is unchanged because the failed attempt never committed. It extracts the window of hwm minus 2 hours, so it never reuses the failed attempt's window.

q12.answer: It re-reads all orders created on each mismatched created_at day from the replica, in full and not just changed rows. They are loaded into stg.orders and applied with the same guarded MERGE into dw.orders, all mismatched days in one transaction. It does not touch the nightly high-water mark. It only logs to etl.run_log with kind=reconcile.
